_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'English Syllabus, Grade 10-12' (2013, published by CDC) — Grade 10, Topics 10.1-10.5. Topic, sub-topic and Specific Outcome statements only; the 'Content' (Knowledge/Skills/Values) columns are omitted, consistent with the approach used for the other 2013 OBC subjects in this app — though for this syllabus the Content column is itself often the worked example illustrating the grammar/writing point (e.g. a sample sentence), not a separate elaboration, since Structure outcomes are very fine-grained already. Two reconstructions were needed: under 10.3 (Composition), the sub-topic 'Writing Speeches' (10.3.8) has its Content column text interleaved with the adjacent 'Writing Minutes' (10.3.7) sub-topic in the source PDF's extraction (a column-scrambling issue matching the same pattern seen in other CDC OBC syllabi); its outcome was reconstructed from the one clearly attributable skill statement ('making speech introduction') as 'Write a speech of introduction'. Sub-topic 10.5.5 does not exist in the source — Structure jumps from 10.5.4 (Noun Phrases and Clauses) to 10.5.6 (Relative Clauses), a genuine gap in the original numbering, not an extraction artifact. This file's subject code is 'ENG', matching the CBC_2023 English entries already in this app for Grade 8 and the earlier OBC_2013 Form 3 placeholder — differentiated by curriculum_code and grade_level exactly like every other subject with entries in both curricula. The syllabus organizes content by Grade only, not by Term, so all of Grade 10 is modeled as a single term here.

Write advanced narrative compositions
Write advanced essays in other subjects

Write book reviews

sub_topics.name: 10.5.2 Parts of Speech: Verbs and Expressions Followed by -ing

competencies.description: Use the -ing form after expressions such as can't help, can't stand, it's no good, it's no use, be worth
Recognise the difference in meaning of similar constructions using verbs followed by either the infinitive or -ing: allow, permit, remember, forget, try, regret, mean (signify), stop, need, go on
Use 'some' meaning one or another
Use infinitive phrases as objects
Recognise the meaning of 'that' clauses and infinitive phrases when used as subjects
Recognise the meaning of the possessive adjectives used with -ing phrases
Use noun phrases in apposition to other nouns
Use relative pronouns in defining relative clauses such as 'who' with subjects that are people
Use relative pronouns in non-defining relative clauses such as 'who' with subjects that are people
Use 'which' with subjects that are things
Use 'whom' or 'who' with objects that are people
Use 'which' with objects that are things
Use preposition + 'whom' with objects that are people
Use preposition + 'which' with objects that are things
Use 'whose' to show possession (especially for people)
Use "the + comparative...the + comparative" to express parallel increase
Use 'now that' to express reason
Use 'seeing that' to express reason
Use participial phrases to express reason
Use conjunction + participial phrases to express time
Use 'no sooner...than' with inversion as an alternative to 'as soon as'
Use phrases containing the perfect participle when one action precedes another
Use structures to express contrast (apart from, besides, although, while, despite, in spite of, instead of + present participle)
Use "(the) one...the other" to express contrast
Use 'if' (for recognition only) to express contrast
Use adjective + as/though (for recognition only) to express contrast
Use 'no matter' to express contrast
Construct conditional sentences with 'but for' to express negative condition
Construct conditional sentences with 'provided/providing that'
Construct conditional sentences with '(that) suppose/supposing'
Construct conditional sentences with 'if only' to indicate hope or regret
Recognise the inverted forms of conditional sentences
Use and apply question tags appropriately
Use the active and passive voice
